C001: Translate "The treaty fails unless the Senate consents." Which way does the arrow run, and what is the trap?
C002: "Every country that has hosted the program for more than five years has seen an increase in favorable opinion. Country Z has seen no increase." What follows about Z? (Naming the rule is no longer tested, since Lesson #11; test the logic only.)
C003: How do you test whether an answer choice is a necessary assumption? Apply it: "Four-day-week companies report higher job satisfaction, so a four-day week would raise satisfaction at Meridian." Why is "four-day-week employees work fewer total hours" not necessary?
C004: On RC inference and main-point questions, why are "true-ish" or "the author would agree" answers often wrong, and which answer type usually wins?
C005: Translate "The ceasefire will hold unless the border is closed." Which statement is valid: (i) "border closed → ceasefire fails" or (ii) "border NOT closed → ceasefire holds"? Give the contrapositive and a counterexample to the invalid one.
C006: A panel of 2 is chosen at random from 5 officers, 3 of whom are Political-cone. What is P(both Political)? Why is 0.6 × 0.6 = 36% wrong?
C007: Which is correct, and why: "Walking into the embassy, the flag was visible above the gate" vs. "Walking into the embassy, she saw the flag above the gate"? Why doesn't passive voice rescue "Having walked into the embassy, the flag was seen by her…"?
C008: Country X makes 6 grain OR 6 cloth per day; Country Y makes 4 grain OR 2 cloth. Who has the comparative advantage in each good, and why can trade help both even though X is better at both?
C009: Translate "No attaché may enter the compound without clearance." Give the arrow, the contrapositive, and the trap.
C010: "Every treaty the Senate ratifies was first approved by the Committee. No treaty the Committee approved is opposed by the Secretary of State. The Pacific accord is a treaty and the Secretary opposes it." What must be true, and why are "never submitted to the Committee" and "the Senate will never ratify it" wrong?
C011: What did McCulloch v. Maryland (1819) decide? Name the two holdings and the constitutional basis for each.
C012: Country A makes 12 tractors OR 24 tons of grain per day; Country B makes 5 tractors OR 15 tons of grain. Who has the comparative advantage in tractors, and what trade price (grain per tractor) leaves both better off? What is the first step of the method?
C013: Write each as an arrow and contrast them: (a) "The talks continue unless the delegation walks out." (b) "No ambassador may sign the accord without the Secretary's approval." Why does "unless" put a NOT on the if-side but "without" doesn't?
C014: A lawyer is faster than her assistant at both typing and legal work. Why should she still delegate the typing? Apply the same logic to a superpower and a smaller ally.
C015: Socrates says "the unexamined life is not worth living." Write it as a conditional with its contrapositive. Does the unqualified wording prove that examination is the source of all value?
C016: Describe the Socratic method in three steps, and say what the two kinds of counterexample show. Apply it to "Courage is staying at your post."
C017: "The talks continue unless the delegation walks out." Is the contrapositive safe with no extra assumption? Give it, and say what the converse would add.
C018: Of 5 officers, 3 are Political-cone. Two are chosen at random without replacement. What is P(at least one is Political)? Before any numbers: what is the complement event in words?
C019: Given the arrow "no revocation → embassy stays open", write its converse, inverse and contrapositive. Which one is equivalent, and why are the other two traps?
C020: Compute 4/6 × 3/5 with no calculator and no decimals. Why is converting 4/6 to 0.6 a trap?
C021: Take "If A, then B". Name the four moves and say which are valid: (1) A, so B. (2) not B, so not A. (3) B, so A. (4) not A, so not B.
C022: "A state receives the grant only if it passes the audit." Write the arrow. Does "only if" tell you that passing the audit is sufficient? How is "only if" different from "if and only if"? Give a quick test.
C023: "Every ally voted yes. Every committee member voted yes." What follows about allies and committee members? What is the chain rule, and what do you get from a chain's contrapositive?
C024: "Most analysts back plan A. Most analysts back plan B." (same group.) Must someone back both, and why? For 30 delegates, where most attended the morning session and most the afternoon, what is the smallest number who attended both? Show the arithmetic.
C025: "Of 30 delegates, most attended the morning session and most attended the afternoon session. A delegate is admitted to the closing dinner only if that delegate attended both sessions." Must at least two have attended both? Must at least two have been admitted? Why?
C026: Write the real logical opposite of each: (a) "All the delegates agreed." (b) "No delegate agreed." (c) "Some delegates agreed." (d) "Most delegates agreed." Why is "none agreed" not the opposite of "all agreed"?
C027: Write the opposite of (a) "If the talks collapse, the aid is frozen." (b) "No cable is released without approval." Why is "If the talks collapse, the aid is NOT frozen" not the opposite of (a)?
C028: How do you use the negation test on a necessary-assumption question, and why is an answer that merely restates a premise a trap? Apply it: "Every delegate who received the briefing packet voted for the resolution. So the packet persuaded delegates to vote for it." What kind of choice is necessary?
C029: On a necessary-assumption question, what do you write down BEFORE reading the choices? Apply it: "The ministry sold every armored car it owned last spring. None of the twelve cars it bought in 2020 appears in last spring's sales records. So none of those twelve cars was armored." What is the gap, and which three kinds of wrong answer do you reject?
C030: On a sufficient-assumption ("the conclusion follows logically if…") or principle-justify question, what must the right answer do? Apply it: "If the aid budget is cut, most rural clinics will close. The aid budget has been cut. So most rural patients will lose access to care." Which choice justifies it: (i) "If most rural clinics close, most rural patients will lose access to care" or (ii) "If most rural clinics stay open, most rural patients will keep access to care"? Name the trap.
C031: "Critics say the new embassy compound is a waste of money. They are mistaken. The compound replaces three leased buildings, and within a decade the savings on rent will exceed its cost." What is the main conclusion, and what is the trap answer?
C032: What is your LR pacing rule, and what are the five trap answer types you check every wrong choice against?
C033: Athens says: "Justice is only talked about between equals in power." Write it as one arrow with the requirement on the THEN side. Is "If we are equals in power, then we may talk about justice" the same claim? What does the right arrow let you conclude about Melos?
C034: In the Melian Dialogue, what is Athens' position, and how does it answer each of the Melians' three appeals? Does Thucydides endorse it? Separate "should" from "will".
C035: An RC passage says an author narrates speech X, then event Y directly after it, draws no explicit connection, but "the placement is deliberate." Why is "X caused Y" a trap, and what is the supported inference?
C036: A frost destroys half of this year's coffee crop. What happens to the price and to the quantity traded, and which curve shifts and which quantity moves along?
C037: A fad adds buyers at every price while a frost cuts supply at the same time. What happens to the price, and what happens to the quantity traded? Is the equilibrium price an average of what buyers and sellers want?
C038: "Fare-free weekends raised transit ridership by 30 percent, so fewer cars came downtown." Before any answer choice, state the gap in one line. What is the necessary assumption, and what happens when you negate it?
C039: The staff-to-case ratio is 3 to 5, and there are 40 cases. How many staff? Then: 40 lawyers split between two offices in the ratio 3 to 5. How many in each? What do you do FIRST in both?
C040: 4 officers clear 18 cases in 3 days. How long do 6 officers take to clear 54 cases? And if the number of officers goes from 4 to 6, what is the percent change in officers, and in the days needed for the same job?
C041: Which branch holds the constitutional power to set tariffs, and how can a President impose them anyway? Give one reason Congress might regret delegating that power.
C042: Who imposed the 1973 oil embargo, against whom and why? What happened to the price, and in supply-and-demand terms what shifted?
C043: If sanctions or tariffs remove a large share of a big supplier's oil from the market, what shifts, what slides along, and what happens to the price and the quantity traded? Why does the pump price jump, and why does that worry a government before an election?
C044: Write the real logical opposite of (a) "The delegation will bring a translator or a legal adviser." (b) "The embassy was closed and the staff was evacuated." Does plain "or" allow both parts to be true? State the swap rule.
C045: What are the three steps of a GRE Text Completion item, and why does step 2 matter? Apply it: "A single forged signature can ______ an otherwise valid contract, stripping it of its legal force." (preclude / vitiate / obviate)
C046: "A grant is awarded only if the proposal passed both the technical review and the budget review. No proposal passes the budget review unless it was submitted before the deadline. Harbor's proposal was submitted after the deadline." Which must be true, and why is "Harbor would have received a grant had it been on time" wrong?
C047: A supply drop of 8% hits a market where buyers cut their quantity by 4% for every 10% price rise. By what percent must the price rise to clear the market? Does the price rise more or less than the quantity falls, and why? Name three things that make demand inelastic.
C048: Is the product of two consecutive integers always, sometimes or never even? Is 7,482 divisible by 3? By 9? Give the prime factorization of 84. If n² is odd, must n be odd?
C049: "Commentators claim that suspending the gasoline tax for the summer will lower pump prices. That claim is mistaken. Refiners cannot expand output within a single summer, and drivers will keep buying about as much whatever the price. So sellers can raise their own price by the amount of the tax cut, and the pump price will barely move. Besides, the suspension would cost the treasury billions." What is the main conclusion, and why is "Sellers will always raise their prices by the amount of any tax cut" wrong?
C050: What is Glaucon's ring (of Gyges) argument in *Republic* II, and what does it claim about why people are just? What does he ask Socrates to prove?
C051: Name Glaucon's three kinds of goods and where he wants justice placed; then give Socrates' reply in one idea (the three parts of the soul) and say why the ring cannot touch it. What is the strongest objection (the psychopath)?
C052: On the GRE Analyze an Issue task, what separates a 4 from a 6, and what should a thesis for "discuss the extent to which you agree or disagree" look like?
C053: In "Fare-free weekends raised transit ridership by 30 percent, so fewer cars came downtown", which clause is the conclusion, and where does the gap in a necessary-assumption item usually sit? Why is "the weekends caused the 30 percent rise" a trap?
C054: "Everyone agrees that a government should not spend money on projects whose benefits go mainly to people who are already wealthy. The proposed Harbor Tunnel would be paid for entirely out of public funds. Thus, the government should not build the Harbor Tunnel." What is the conclusion, what is the gap (a term shift), and what is the necessary assumption? Why is "the tunnel would be paid for entirely out of public funds" a trap?
C055: "Some analysts argue that raising the retirement age will inevitably hurt manual workers. But a higher retirement age could be paired with a partial early-pension option that protects them while still saving the pension fund money. So a higher retirement age need not hurt manual workers." What is the main conclusion, and why is "Raising the retirement age will not hurt manual workers" wrong?
C056: "Among first-year students who joined the mentoring program, 9 percent dropped out; among those who did not, 14 percent did. The dean concludes the program reduces first-year dropout." State the conclusion (with its direction), the gap, the necessary assumption, and what happens when you negate it. Which choice is the restated premise, and what does ITS negation do?
C057: What is a sufficient assumption, and how do you find it? Apply it: "Anyone who completes the safety course is assigned to the night shift. Priya has worked here for three years. Therefore, Priya will be assigned to the night shift." What must you add? Why does "too strong" stop being a flaw on these items?
C058: "Every report the ambassador signs goes to the Secretary. This cable is a report the ambassador drafted. So this cable will go to the Secretary." Which bridge works: (i) every report she drafts, she signs; (ii) every report she signs, she drafts; (iii) any report she does not sign does not go to the Secretary? Then: "no document negotiated on the public's behalf should stay secret unless publishing it would harm national security." Write the rule as an arrow and say which assumption makes "publish the agreement" follow.
C059: What is your method for a two-blank text completion item? Apply it: "Although the minister's critics dismissed his proposal as (i)____, even they conceded that its central analysis of the budget gap was (ii)____." (i) fatuous / trenchant / exigent; (ii) trenchant / spurious / perfidious. How can a fatuous proposal contain a trenchant analysis?
C060: A town's grain sells 100 sacks at 10 coins. A ceiling of 6 cuts supply to 60 sacks while buyers want 140. Name the 80-sack gap, the 40 lost trades, and say what deadweight loss is.
C061: Who bears most of a tax, and does it matter who legally pays it? How does elasticity change the deadweight loss?
C062: Argument: 'Since bike lanes were painted on Harbor Street, shop sales fell 8%. Owners rightly blame the lanes. Removing them will restore sales.' What is the MAIN conclusion, and which necessary assumption states the gap in general form? Why is 'sales on other streets did not fall similarly' not necessary?
C063: Aristotle, Politics: what two questions sort the six regimes, which are the sound and deviant forms of rule by one, few and many, and why is his 'democracy' a deviation?
C064: Write the shape of a 6-level thesis in one sentence, and what must the 'except when' clause do? Test it on: 'Leaders should follow their own judgment rather than popular opinion.'
C065: Write a GRE Issue thesis in one sentence of 40 words or fewer. What shape does it take, and what must the 'except when' do? (Nov 6 prompt: governments and future generations)
C066: A prompt says governments should put X AHEAD OF Y. Why is 'if governments did it always, no citizen would ever be served' a weak line of attack, and what is the better move? Also: how do you test each example?
C067: Why can't a democratic government easily act for future generations, and what is the sharpest way to state when it still may? (Consent and the unborn)
C068: How do you find the main conclusion and label roles in an argument? Apply it: A critic says X is a waste because the count was low; the author says the count was taken in exam week so it cannot show X is a waste, and so the council should wait for a normal month. What is the main conclusion, what is the role of the count cannot show X is a waste, and what is a concession?
C069: Define stock and flow and say how they are linked. A country has debt of 30 trillion; the deficit fell from 1.5 to 1.0 trillion; a politician says we have cut the debt by a third. Right or wrong? A lake loses 1 million liters a month net; the town cuts the outflow by half a million: does it stop shrinking?
C070: GRE Sentence Equivalence: how many answers do you pick, what must be true of them, and what are the three traps?
C071: How do you find the GCD and LCM of 12 and 18 from prime factors? Give the check. What does n leaves remainder 4 when divided by 6 mean, and what remainder does n + 5 leave?
C072: A and B go together and an author concludes 'A causes B'. List the five other explanations the author must rule out, and say which one is the general gap on a causal necessary-assumption item. Why is regression to the mean a form of coincidence?
C073: Original item: the 10 lowest-scoring of 40 schools got a free-breakfast program; their reading scores rose 6 points; the superintendent says breakfast raised scores. Which kind of answer weakens it most, and why do these choices fail: (a) the other 30 schools were unchanged, (b) attendance rose, (c) the 10 schools stayed below the district average?
C074: US treaties: who negotiates, who ratifies, by what vote, and what do presidents use to avoid that vote? Why is 'executive order' the wrong name for it?
C075: GRE Verbal: name four reversing signals (one hidden) and four continuing signals, and say what 'not merely critical but ___' tells you about the blank. Fill: 'Although the senator is usually ___ in public, her speech was strikingly blunt' (circumspect / bellicose / garrulous).
C076: Name the two feedback-loop types, the quick test for telling them apart, and what a delay does to a balancing loop. Give one example of each (bank run, thermostat, housing).
C077: Give the five exponent rules via 'count the factors' (multiply, divide, zero, negative, power of a power), then do: (a) -3^2 vs (-3)^2, (b) 2^-1, (c) sqrt(75) and sqrt(48), (d) 16^(1/2).
C078: Parallel flaw drill: 'No hospital can qualify for the safety award without reporting every infection incident. Westbrook reports every incident. So Westbrook will qualify.' Name the flaw, and say how you tell it from a valid contrapositive and a valid 'only ... earn' argument in the choices.
C079: Machiavelli, The Prince ch. 17: state his claim WITH its hedge, his reason for distrusting love, and what a feared ruler must avoid.
C080: A thesis says a leader may defy popularity to be effective, 'for the sake of the people'. The strongest counterargument is Stalin and Mao. What kind of limit ('except when ...') answers it, and what is the form and length of the thesis?
C081: An author reports a view ('commentators claim X shows Y'), says 'this claim is mistaken', gives a premise, then a 'so' sentence. Which sentence is the main conclusion, how do you test it, and what do you check about the choices?
C082: GRE 'select ALL that apply' passage item: what is the first thing you do, and how do you judge each choice?
